product_backlog.title: To-Do List Core Features
product_backlog.description: Core functionality for managing to-do lists and tasks across 5 sprints.
As a single user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
product_backlog.title: Create To-Do List
acceptance_criteria: Given the home page is open, When the user enters a list name and clicks create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.

product_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.
product_backlog.title: Add Task to List
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list, When the user enters task description and adds it, Then the task appears under that list.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can add tasks to lists.

product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists, When the user clicks complete/incomplete toggle, Then the task state updates visually.
product_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track progress.

acceptance_criteria: Given a task exists, When the user clicks delete on the task, Then the task is removed from the list.
product_backlog.title: Delete Task
product_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove unwanted items.

acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list exists, When the user clicks delete list, Then the list and all its tasks are removed.
product_backlog.title: Delete Entire List
product_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete lists.

acceptance_criteria: Given lists and tasks exist, When the user views the main page, Then all lists and tasks are shown with completed tasks visually distinguished.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users have a clear dashboard overview.
product_backlog.title: View Lists and Tasks Dashboard
product_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to see all my lists and tasks with visual distinction for completed items so that I have a clear overview.

sprint_backlog.description: As a single user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.

acceptance_criteria: Given an existing to-do list, When the user enters task description and adds it, Then the task appears under that list.
sprint_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can add tasks to lists.
dod_checks: User can add tasks to an existing list via UI
Tests cover task creation API and logic
sprint_backlog.test_approach: Pytest tests for adding tasks to lists.

sprint_backlog.approach: Extend Flask API and HTML/JS UI to support adding tasks to lists, displaying tasks under their respective lists.

decision_log.title: Sprint 1 Architecture & Tech Stack Selection
decision_log.decision: Selected Flask + Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS + In-memory store for Sprint 1 MVP. Validated technical feasibility for US-0001 and US-0002.
decision_log.rationale: Minimizes setup friction, meets all functional requirements, allows rapid iteration across 5 sprints.

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team
> produced.** Its entire value is being byte-identical across runs, so results are
> comparable across Horseless Carriage versions over time. If the scenario itself

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.
